candidates.title: 1Password reports 21% productivity lift from Codex
candidates.summary: The company integrated Codex across implementation, PR review, testing, incidents, and internal tooling while keeping security controls in the workflow.
candidates.what_changed: 1Password says its core Codex cohort improved engineering productivity by about 21% and reduced median pull-request cycle time by nearly 11%.
candidates.why_it_matters: The case study reinforces a practical pattern: agent adoption works best when it is integrated into an existing delivery and security system rather than bolted on as a separate chat tool.

candidates.title: Agentic Harness Engineering turns traces into harness improvements
candidates.summary: The paper frames coding-agent reliability as an observability and runtime-design problem, then proposes automatically evolving harness components from trajectory evidence.
candidates.what_changed: This work argues that the next optimization target for coding agents is not only the model, but the **harness around the model**.
candidates.why_it_matters: It suggests a future in which agent runtimes are evaluated and iterated like production systems: instrumented, compared, regressed, and improved from trace evidence rather than intuition.

candidates.title: A source-code study finds coding agents converging on seven harness subsystems
candidates.summary: An audit of eleven production coding agents identifies recurring runtime patterns across loops, tools, context, safety, orchestration, and extensibility.
candidates.what_changed: A source-code study of eleven production coding agents maps the runtime around the model into seven recurring subsystems: the loop, model integration, tools, context and memory, permissions, orchestration, and extension surfaces.
candidates.why_it_matters: This is useful architecture evidence for teams building internal agents. The model is one replaceable component; the durable engineering value increasingly sits in the runtime that controls how the model acts.

candidates.title: GitHub HydraFusion routes coding work across multiple models
candidates.summary: HydraFusion plans, drafts, critiques, revises, and selectively escalates tasks across models instead of binding a workflow to one checkpoint.
candidates.what_changed: HydraFusion is GitHub's research preview for runtime model orchestration inside Copilot.
candidates.why_it_matters: Model selection is becoming a **runtime scheduling problem**. For engineering teams, that opens a new optimization surface: quality, latency, and cost can be traded at the subtask level instead of the session level.
